schemaPlaceholder: empty = like the latest event channel

raid.label: Raid signup
raid.hint: Default channel a new raid event is posted to when nothing else is chosen while creating it.

logs.label: Log evaluation
logs.hint: When someone posts a Warcraft Logs link here, the bot offers the evaluation via a button. Several channels possible.

application.label: Applications
application.hint: Channel where new applications are posted as a thread.

eventCategories.label: Event categories
eventCategories.hint: Discord categories whose channels hold raid events. Roles, loot addon and sheet per category are under Settings › Categories.

lib.archivedByHand: moved to the archive by hand
lib.tipNothing: No topic, no purpose, no event.
lib.deleteWarning: #{name} belongs to the upcoming event “{title}” ({date}) — its signup message is lost with it.

rights.cantViewTip: The bot role lacks the “View channel” permission in #{name}. Selectable, but it only takes effect once the permission is set in Discord.
rights.cantSendTip: The bot role lacks the “Send messages” permission in #{name}.
rights.readsTip: The bot sees #{name} and can reply there.

page.title: Channels
page.pickServer: Choose a server above to manage its channels.
page.offlineSub: Channels and permissions come live from Discord — without a connection the list stays empty.
page.noManageSub: The bot role lacks “Manage channels”. Renaming, archiving and creating fail until the permission is set in Discord.
page.waitingTip: Archived channels waiting to be deleted
page.waitingSub: {overdue} of them longer than {days} days. Nothing is ever deleted automatically.
page.figChannelsSub: All channels of the server outside the archive.
page.figPastPick: Click selects them all — then “Archive” below.
page.figPastSub: Channels whose event is over and that are not in the archive yet.
page.figArchive: In the archive, waiting to be deleted
page.figArchiveSub: Marked yellow after {days} days. Nothing is ever deleted automatically — only by an admin in the archive.
page.purposesSub: What the bot uses which channels for (log, application channel …). On the channel itself they are in the tooltip.
page.allPurposesSub: What the bot uses which channels for — all at a glance.

jobs.archiveText: They move to “{category}”, nobody can post there any more. Nothing is deleted — an admin does that later in the archive.

archive.empty: No archive category yet. Archived channels move there and nobody can post in them any more — they are only deleted when an admin does it here.
archive.title: Archive
archive.hintSub: After {days} days a waiting channel is marked yellow. Nothing is ever deleted automatically.
archive.overdueSub: In the archive for more than {days} days.
archive.deleteSub: Delete from Discord for good — confirm with the name.

deleteDialog.note: The channel and all messages in it are gone afterwards — this cannot be undone in Discord either.

archiveSettings.title: Archive settings
archiveSettings.hintSub: From then on an archived channel shows yellow on the Channels page and in the open tasks of the dashboard. Nothing is ever deleted automatically.

schemaDialog.reset: {name}: names like the latest event channel again.
schemaDialog.schemaSub: Applies to every new event channel of this category – creating an event in the web and in the bot, quick create, /kanal anlegen. Empty: like the latest event channel, only date, weekday and raid are replaced.
schemaDialog.raidSub: For {raid}, when the event itself brings no raid (quick create).
schemaDialog.templateSub: New channels take over the permissions, topic and slowmode of this channel. Without a choice they copy the latest event channel of the category.

bulk.renameHint: Channels with a conflict stay as they are.
bulk.conflictSub: The name is empty or already belongs to another channel. This channel is skipped.
bulk.noEventKeepSub: The channel belongs to no known event — without its date the name cannot be derived, so it stays.
bulk.noEventEmptySub: The channel belongs to no known event, the date parts stay empty.

edit.title: Edit #{name}
edit.rightsCategorySub: The channel takes over the permissions of its category. Moving it changes nothing about that — the permissions stay as they are.
edit.rightsOwnSub: The channel has its own permissions, different from the category. Role permissions are managed in Discord.

tree.pastSub: {title} · {date}. Archiving clears the channel out of the list — nothing is deleted.
tree.renameSub: Or double-click the name. Enter saves, Esc discards.
tree.editSub: Name, topic, category, slowmode, permissions, archive.
tree.duplicateSub: Clone with permissions, topic and slowmode in the same category.
tree.deleteSub: Delete from Discord for good — confirm with the name. To put it aside, archive instead.
tree.doubleClick: Double-click a name to edit it
tree.noChannels: No channels found — is the bot connected?
tree.ownSchemaSub: {schema} — applies to every new event channel of this category.
tree.schemaOwn: New event channels are named by {schema}.
tree.schemaNone: New event channels are named like the latest event channel. Set a schema of its own here.

purposeList.label: Purposes
purposeList.purposeSub: What the bot uses the channels for. Hovering the name explains what it does there.
purposeList.statusSub: Whether the purpose is set, the channel still exists and the bot may do there what it has to.
purposeList.openSettingsSub: Purposes are settings — changing them needs write access to settings.
purposeList.warningsSub: Channel missing or the bot may not read/post there — details in the status.
purposeList.dialogTitle: What the bot uses which channels for

purposeDialog.title: Assign {label}
purposeDialog.noteBefore: Saved as a setting — can also be changed under

createDialog.title: Create channel
createDialog.assignNowSub: The new channel takes on a purpose right away. For purposes with only one channel it replaces the previous one.

duplicateDialog.title: Duplicate channel
duplicateDialog.name: Name of the duplicate
duplicateDialog.rightsSub: The permissions of the original, role by role.
duplicateDialog.categorySub: The duplicate lands in {where}, like the original.
duplicateDialog.noPurposeSub: What the bot uses the original for does not come along — assign the duplicate afterwards via “Assign purpose”.

quick.title: Create channels
quick.withEventTip: Every new channel gets an event on its day – with the default template and signup of the category.
quick.templateSub: Size, tanks/healers and signup deadline come from the category's default template. Signup via {source}. Change it: Settings → Categories.
quick.noTemplateSub: The category has no default template – the event gets the values of the rule set. Signup via {source}. Set it: Settings → Categories.
quick.existsSub: A channel with this name is already there (or appears twice in this series) — it is skipped.
quick.templateChannelSub: The new channels take over the permissions, topic and slowmode of this channel. Without a choice they copy the latest event channel of the category – only a category without an event channel gets plain text channels.
quick.remember: Remember schema, raid and template for “{name}”
